newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks mixed, seen stronger next week.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks mixed, seen stronger next week.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks traded mixed to softer on Friday, but brokers said they expected the market to resume its march upwards next week as investor sentiment was still strong.
Th key industrial index shed 15.56 points to close at 10,964.54, pulled down by losses on a couple of major counters. It rose 389.22 points on the week.

"The market quietened down a little bit today, bascially it is a temporary breather after a hectic week and I think the market is going to go up again next week. I think we are going to see the index hitting 11,000 soon," a broker said.
He added a tightening this week of foreign exchange controls on dual-listed stocks had not yet had much effect on trade, but said foreigners were likely to trade more cautiously.

Notable among Friday's losers were bankers Barclays, which dropped 50 cents to 3,150, food group Natfoods, down 45 cents to 455, hotel and mining conglomerate TA Holdings lost 20 cents to 210 and clothing retailer Edgars traded 10 cents down at 810.
Several counters traded firmer, notably newly-listed vegetable firm Interfresh which rose 30 cents to 280. Brokers said its debut continued to attract much attention from buyers.
Merchant bank FMB leapt 100 cents to 5,200, clothing retailer Truworths climbed 25 cents to 1,025 as did sugar grower Hippo to 1,650 and glass firm PGI gained 10 cents to 640.
Minings were quiet with gold producers Ashanti and Falgold unchanged despite a firmer bullion price. The mining index was unmoved at 1,014.88.
